transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Peregrine Head of ML), Oliver Park (Peregrine Platform), Sonia Patel (Peregrine Privacy)

Summary (auto): POC scoping for Peregrine AI to validate Redwood for high-throughput chat + tool-calling workflows, decide between Hosted vs Dedicated, and run benchmarks focused on latency and cost per token.

[00:00] Avery Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Avery, AE at Redwood — I'll kick things off. Diego from SE will cover technical bits and bench plan.
[00:15] Maya Singh: Hey thanks, Maya here. Quick context: we're building an assistant for our analytics platform. Primary goal is fast interactive chat for analysts with tool calls into our query service and structured JSON responses for downstream ingestion.
[00:32] Oliver Park: Yeah and we have about 200k monthly active analysts, peak concurrency around 150-200, average session length 8 minutes. Avg tokens per request maybe 900 but we have a long tail with 2k-4k.
[00:50] Diego Morales: Cool that's helpful. Two immediate scoping questions: what's your success criteria for the POC, and do you have a preferred timeline?
[01:05] Maya Singh: Success is threefold: 1) latency under 800ms 95th for typical 900 token prompts on interactive mode, 2) reliable function/tool calling latency under 1.2s end-to-end, and 3) structured JSON accuracy above 92% on our eval set. If cost is prohibitive we'd consider quantization.
[01:30] Avery Chen: Great, we'll target those. We typically suggest a small benchmark matrix: hosted (fastest to try), dedicated reserved pool for predictable throughput, and private VPC if you need data isolation. For POC most customers try hosted or dedicated depending on security needs.
[01:55] Sonia Patel: We're evaluating VPC for data residency and KMS integration. SOC2 and SAML SSO are non-negotiable. Can you confirm encryption at rest and KMS support?
[02:12] Diego Morales: Yes — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and we can scope the POC for a VPC egress or dedicated config. For the initial run we'll propose hosted with logging turned off for any PII examples you mark.
[02:30] Maya Singh: Ok sounds pragmatic. On the integration side we use an OpenAI-compatible SDK today; we want minimal code changes. How compatible are Redwood's endpoints and SDKs?
[02:45] Avery Chen: We provide OpenAI-compatible endpoints (same request/response shape) plus official SDKs in Python/TS. We also support function-calling and structured output helpers — small differences around streaming metadata and some Redwood-specific headers. We'll share code snippets.
[03:05] Oliver Park: Do you support the full function-calling spec? We have multi-step tool calls (e.g., query -> enrich -> render table).
[03:20] Diego Morales: Yes, function calling is supported. We also have an examples repo for tool orchestration patterns. For complex multi-step flows we recommend running a small simulated workload to validate KV cache behavior and token reuse.
[03:40] Maya Singh: Token reuse — we saw large cost spikes in our tests because we weren't caching prefixes. How does Redwood handle KV cache and batching?
[03:55] Diego Morales: The runtime has prefix caching and workload-aware batching. For interactive workloads we can tune batching window and target throughput to avoid tail latency. For long-tail 4k prompts we recommend a dedicated instance profile with optimized kernels.
[04:15] Avery Chen: To scope the POC we'll need: traffic profile (peak/avg sessions, token distribution), a labeled eval set for structured output scoring, and your acceptance criteria. We'll run two benchmark types: synthetic openai-compatible traffic and a replay of your sample prompts.
[04:40] Oliver Park: We can provide traffic from staging — about 2k sample prompts, including 150 flagged as PII, we can redact those if needed.
[04:52] Sonia Patel: We'll redact PII before sharing; legal will send a short data sharing addendum.
[05:05] Diego Morales: Good. For bench config: we'll propose runs at 1x, 3x, and 5x expected peak concurrency, measuring p50/p95/p99 latency and tokens/sec. We'll also collect cost per 1k tokens estimate for each config.
[05:30] Maya Singh: For structured output scoring, we need a stable scorer — do you provide eval harness or should we run our own?
[05:45] Diego Morales: We provide a sample eval harness and can run the tests on our Dedicated infra, or we can give you the harness to run in your environment. Many teams prefer we run the official runs so numbers are comparable.
[06:05] Avery Chen: We'll share the harness plus a spreadsheet template for SLOs and results. We'll also include a checklist for security docs (SOC2, ISO, KMS integration steps).
[06:25] Maya Singh: Sounds good. Quick question on streaming: for our UI we rely on server-side streaming with deltas. Are the streaming semantics identical to OpenAI's?
[06:40] Diego Morales: Generally yes — delta streams and event types are the same. Small differences: we include a trace id header and some additional chunk metadata. We'll document the exact stream frames.
[06:55] Oliver Park: Any examples for TypeScript SDK and function-calling with structured output?
[07:05] Diego Morales: We have a repo with a sample app that demonstrates function calling + JSON schema enforcement. We'll link that.
[07:18] Maya Singh: On quantization — if we need to reduce cost, do you offer quantized model variants and what's the quality delta?
[07:30] Diego Morales: Yes, we offer 4-bit/8-bit quant profiles. We typically recommend running a quality regression check; most customers see <3% quality drop on standard LLM tasks but it depends on your eval set. We'll propose a recommended quant profile for your workload after a quick model pass.
[07:55] Sonia Patel: From a compliance POV we need audit logs for prompt/response access. Is there RBAC + logs in Redwood Console?
[08:12] Avery Chen: Yes — Redwood Console offers token-level cost/latency breakdowns, RBAC, and audit logs. For Private deployments we also support longer retention and external SIEM hooks.
[08:30] Maya Singh: Great. Let's talk succeed criteria and timeline — we want to decide by mid-March and run a POC in March. Is that feasible?
[08:45] Avery Chen: Yes. Proposed timeline: this week share pricing + harness, Peregrine shares traffic samples by Tue 2026-02-24, Redwood seeds a benchmark run week of 2026-03-02, results and review the following week, decision by 2026-03-15.
[09:05] Oliver Park: That aligns with our internal timeline. For the benchmark run, can we reserve dedicated capacity during the test window? We want to avoid noisy neighbor artifacts.
[09:20] Diego Morales: We can reserve a dedicated test pool for the run — small fee for reserved GPU cluster during bench. We'll include the option in the pricing doc.
[09:35] Maya Singh: On metrics: we want p95 latency for 900 token prompts <800ms and p95 for function invocation end-to-end <1.2s. Also cost per 10k tokens target under $0.45.
[09:55] Diego Morales: We'll include those in the bench acceptance criteria and try to match. Note cost targets depend on model and quantization. We'll provide a cost matrix per model/quant config.
[10:12] Oliver Park: Regarding SDK migration: we currently use openai.ChatCompletion calls, will the calls be a drop-in?
[10:25] Avery Chen: Pretty much drop-in. We'll provide a shim collection and example diff for minimal changes. For advanced features like structured output, we recommend using our schema helpers.
[10:40] Maya Singh: For structured JSON responses we need schema validation and fallbacks when the model returns invalid JSON. Any built-in tooling?
[10:52] Diego Morales: We have structured-output utilities that validate and optionally post-process (repair heuristics). We'll include those in the SDK. But the POC should include your real evals to measure repair rate.
[11:10] Sonia Patel: Legal note — we'll need indemnity language and a data handling appendix if we route any PII through hosted. Prefer Private if PII processed.
[11:25] Avery Chen: Understood. We'll mark options in the addendum and provide private deployment pricing.
[11:40] Maya Singh: Ok let's capture next steps.
[11:45] Diego Morales: Action items recap: Diego will publish benchmark harness + runbook link; Avery will send pricing and Dedicated vs Hosted comparison; Peregrine to share sample prompts and traffic profile; Sonia to confirm compliance doc list.
[12:05] Oliver Park: We'll aim to have samples in by Tue. Also can Diego share an example benchmark report from a recent customer with similar concurrency patterns?
[12:18] Diego Morales: Yes, sanitized report with metrics and config. I'll include it in the follow-up email.
[12:30] Maya Singh: One more question: do you support automatic fallback policies (e.g., if dedicated pool saturated fallback to hosted smaller model)?
[12:45] Avery Chen: Yes — the smart routing layer can failover by policy (region, tier, size). We'll propose a fallback plan for the POC.
[12:58] Sonia Patel: Thanks all, legal will review the addendum and reach out.
[13:05] Avery Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the pricing doc, harness, and links to SDK examples.
[13:15] Maya Singh: Thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.

References shared during call (in chat):
- Benchmark harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness (link shared)
- Pricing + Dedicated options doc: https://redwood.ai/peregrine/poc-pricing (to be sent)
- Example benchmark spreadsheet: https://sheets.redwood.ai/poc-template (template)

Notes about transcription: names and product terms occasionally garbled (e.g., Redwood Dedicatedy, KV cache spelled as K-V cash), filler words and crosstalk present. Transcript aligned to ~52 minute call by sampling key timestamps.
